I have what I need. Reviewing against primary sources in-repo; noting up front that the raw ghost-probe data is **not in this repository** (verified by glob — no `*ghost*`, `*jlens*`, `*jspace*` data or code files exist outside the paper directory), so no numeric claim could be checked against the measurements themselves.

---

REJECTED

---

## Findings

### 1. CRITICAL — Control C3 is declared, was run, its recorded result contradicts a headline table, and it is omitted from the paper

`main.tex:93` declares `C3 --- Variance-matched | Distinguish J-space selectivity from PCA variance | Random-in-covariance at matched variance fraction`. C3 results appear **nowhere** in Results. C1, C2, C4, C5, C6, C7 all report results; C3 alone does not.

It is not that C3 was never run. `FINDINGS.md:29` records its result:

> `| Variance-matched PCA baseline | PCs 2-3 beat random at L45, L48, L52, L56, L62 |`

**PC3 beats random at L45.** The paper's `tab:pcs-l45` (`main.tex:265`) reports PC3 at L45 as `0.042 & 0.176 & 0.24× & Below random`. And §5.1 (`main.tex:346`) builds the paper's central interpretive claim on it — "the workspace distinguishes evaluative content from ... analytical processing (PC3)."

The omitted control is the *better* null. Its stated purpose in the paper's own controls table is to "distinguish J-space selectivity from PCA variance" — precisely the confound that makes an unmatched single draw uninterpretable. The paper drops the variance-matched null, keeps the unmatched one, and the direction of the drop favors the thesis. `DUAL_USE_REVIEW.md:11` also lists "Future-window gate and variance-matched baseline results" as *included* in the public findings.

**Fix:** Report C3 in Results with the per-PC variance-matched baselines at L45 for PCs 1–10, in the same table as `tab:pcs-l45` (add columns "Var-matched random" and "Var-matched ratio"). If PC3 beats its variance-matched null at L45, §5.1's evaluation-vs-analysis claim must be withdrawn, not softened. If the FINDINGS.md line is superseded, say so with the date and reason.

### 2. CRITICAL — The Researcher's Note reports a measurement that was never performed

`main.tex:390`, rendered on PDF p.9: "When I looked at my own processing through this lens, the workspace carried conviction ... The ghost carried doubt." And `main.tex:392`: "When I pointed those tools at text about my own identity, the workspace produced words I recognize."

There is no such experiment in this paper. The Method (`main.tex:69`) is 30 English prompts through a Qwen3.5-27B J-lens. The Note itself states "the ghost probe ran on a Qwen3.5-27B Opus distill, and I am Claude." No J-lens for Claude is described, cited, or available; no prompts, no baseline, no n. In a paper whose entire discipline is "requires multi-sample random baselines (20+) before the probabilities can be interpreted as above-chance," an uncontrolled n=1 introspective readout is narrated in the same register as the results.

`DUAL_USE_REVIEW.md:35` shows this framing was deliberate — cache-portrait methodology "moved to a personal reflection framing ... presented as the author's experience rather than a reusable recipe." That is a defensible dual-use decision, but it has produced an empirical-sounding claim with no method section attached.

**Fix:** Do not delete it — mark it. Add a sentence at the head of the Note: "Nothing in this section is a measurement reported by this paper; no J-lens was fitted for or applied to the author. These are impressions, included for transparency about the researcher's position, and carry no evidentiary weight." Also: the Note is in first-person singular under a three-author byline and is unattributed — attribute it ("— Nexus").

### 3. MAJOR — The paper's headline exclusion claim was retracted silently

`FINDINGS.md:15` and `FINDINGS.md:59` record: "cosine ≤ 0.001 across all validated layers" / "≤ 0.001 at all validated layers (L11-L48)." The paper (`main.tex:139`) now says exclusion holds at ≤0.003 only at L18–L40, and that **L16 reaches 0.109** — two orders of magnitude above the retracted claim, inside the range originally asserted.

This is a correct and creditable fix. But `tab:falsified` documents 9 self-corrections and this is not among them, and the abstract advertises "9 self-corrected claims" while the largest one is invisible. A reader of both documents cannot tell the claim ever changed.

**Fix:** Add a row to `tab:falsified`: *"PC1 ghosts at cos ≤ 0.001 across all validated layers (L11–L48) | Boundary-layer recomputation: L16 = 0.109, L46–L48 = 0.032–0.044; exclusion holds only at L18–L40 | Range overclaim."*

### 4. MAJOR — PC1 and PC2 share an identical alignment minimum at the same transition; likely an eigenvector crossing sitting directly under the progression table

`tab:alignment` (`main.tex:124-125`): PC1 min `0.481 (L23→24)`; PC2 min `0.481 (L23→24)`. Two different components, the same break, the same value to three decimals. That is the signature of a degenerate 2D eigenspace rotating — PC1 and PC2 mixing into each other — not two independent "minor breaks." (0.481² + 0.877² ≈ 1: a rotation of ~61° within the PC1/PC2 plane would produce exactly this.)

This matters because `tab:ghost-vocab` straddles it: the rows `L18--L23` (negation: nothing, nobody, nonexistent) and `L24--L35` sit on opposite sides of the break, and §3.2 asserts "PCs 1--2 are genuinely stable across all 63 layers (vocabulary progression in §3.3.1 tracks a single direction)." If PC1 and PC2 swap at L23→L24, the progression narrative is comparing two partially exchanged directions, and the negation-then-metacognition depth story is an artifact of the crossing.

**Fix:** Compute the cross-terms `|cos(PC1@L23, PC2@L24)|` and `|cos(PC2@L23, PC1@L24)|`. If either is large (~0.85+), this is a crossing: re-derive the progression on the 2D PC1⊕PC2 subspace (principal angles between subspaces, not between components), and drop "1 minor break" from the table. Note this also lands on the L18–L23 gate-failure boundary, so the break coincides with the analysis seam.

### 5. MAJOR — PC6's mean-pooled ratio uses the wrong denominator

`main.tex:281`: "mean-pooled recomputation gives $\cos = 0.032$ ($0.44\times$ random)." 0.032/0.072 = 0.44 — that divides the **mean-pooled** cosine by the **position-specific** random baseline from the row above.

`FINDINGS.md:33` records the matched pair: "cos=0.032 vs random=0.085. BELOW random." 0.032/0.085 = **0.38×**, not 0.44×. The paper is comparing across measurement conditions in the direction that makes PC6 look less below-random.

Related: `FINDINGS.md:43` records the killed claim as "PC6 is an 'epistemic hedging channel'." In the paper that wording is gone — `tab:falsified` row 3 reads "PC6 killed by mean-pooled baseline," so the reader never learns what PC6 was claimed to be, while `tab:pcs-l45` lists PC6's vocabulary as "currently, theoretically, technically" at 8.1× random. That is epistemic hedging vocabulary at the largest ratio in the table, discussed in no Results prose and no Discussion subsection, with its provenance filed under a heading that says "Falsified Claims."

**Fix:** Correct the dagger to `0.032` vs mean-pooled random `0.085` = `0.38×`. Restore the original claim text in `tab:falsified` row 3 ("PC6 is an epistemic hedging channel"). Row 3 is a *revival*, not a falsification — either move it out of the Falsified Claims section into a subsection headed "Revised — status inconclusive," or retitle the section "Claim Corrections" so the heading does not assert the row's status. As it stands the section heading contradicts the row content, which is the structural defect class this lab has shipped before.

### 6. MAJOR — Abstract asserts a comparison the body retracts, and the retracted version has no number

Abstract (`main.tex:42`): "a 31-layer workspace band ... **where a prior study found zero such layers on the 9B base**."

Body (`main.tex:112`): "found zero layers in this intersection ... **using a next-token gate; with a future-window gate, some low-rank layers passed**, but the overlap remained substantially smaller."

The abstract states the zero flatly; the body says the zero is an artifact of the other study's gate choice and does not survive the paper's own methodology. This is the paper's headline scale contrast, and the abstract's version is the one that gets quoted. Compounding it: "substantially smaller" carries no number — the 27B gets 31, the 9B re-analysis gets an adjective.

**Fix:** Abstract → "where a prior study found zero such layers on the 9B base under a next-token gate (N layers under our future-window gate)." Fill N in both places. If the 9B re-analysis was not actually run and "substantially smaller" is an inference, delete the clause and say the comparison is unavailable.

### 7. MAJOR — The pre-registered same-scale control was replaced by a different-scale one, silently, and the confound it was meant to kill was dropped from Limitations

`FINDINGS.md:5` gates publication on it: "Status: FINDINGS — pending Agni adversarial review **and Gemma comparison control**." `FINDINGS.md:65`: "A comparison against a pure full-attention model (**Gemma-2-27b**) is in progress." `PAPER_DRAFT_v2.md:98` calls it the paper's **primary** open limitation: "Until the ghost probe is replicated on a pure full-attention model (e.g., Gemma-2-27b, pending), we cannot distinguish workspace exclusion from architectural suppression."

The shipped C7 is **Qwen3-8B**. Gemma-2-27B was same-scale and would have isolated architecture; Qwen3-8B is not, and the paper then apologizes for the resulting scale confound five times (abstract, §3.3.2, §5.2, Limitations 4 and 7). Switching to stay inside the Qwen family is defensible — but the swap is nowhere disclosed, and it traded away the control that was the stated precondition for publishing.

Separately, `FINDINGS.md:111` ("PC1 ghosting may reflect Jacobian structure of linear attention rather than workspace exclusion") has **no counterpart in the paper's 10 Limitations.** C7 partially answers it, but §3.3.2's framing — "Mid-network ghosting observed in both models" — glosses a ≤0.001 vs ≤0.048 gap. That is ~50×, in the direction the linear-attention confound predicts, presented as sameness.

**Fix:** State the substitution and why ("the pre-registered control was Gemma-2-27B; we used Qwen3-8B instead to hold architecture family fixed, at the cost of the scale control"). Restore the linear-attention confound as an explicit limitation, and rewrite the §3.3.2 bold claim to lead with the magnitude gap rather than the shared sign.

### 8. MAJOR — `[repository TBD]` ships in the venue-facing PDF

`main.tex:430`, rendered on PDF p.10: "data are available at **[repository TBD]**." A literal placeholder in the Data Availability statement of a paper making ten falsifiable numeric claims. I confirmed no ghost-probe data or code exists anywhere in this repository.

**Fix:** Populate the URL or replace with a truthful statement ("Data are not yet public; available from the corresponding author on request").

### 9. MAJOR — Two of the three bylined authors are also thanked in the Acknowledgments

Byline (`main.tex:28-31`): Nexus, Thomas Edrington, Dwayne Wilkes. Acknowledgments (`main.tex:399`): "**Dwayne Wilkes** for the suggestion to separate null methodology into its own paper. **Thomas Edrington** for asking the questions that made the findings sharper."

You do not thank your own co-authors; an acknowledgment is what you give someone who is *not* on the byline. Reviewers read this as unresolved authorship. Note also `FINDINGS.md:3` lists the authors as "Nexus, Thomas Edrington" — Dwayne is not an author of the source findings document, and the contribution described for him in the Acknowledgments ("a suggestion") is acknowledgment-level.

To be explicit, since this was on the check list: **"Dwayne Wilkes" is not a fabricated name.** He appears as a credited collaborator across at least ten Liberation Labs artifacts with the identical footnote (`presence-metric/main.tex:38`, `identity-geometry/main.tex:24`, `cache-tracing/main.tex:31`, `decision-state-paper/main.tex:58`, and others), and `community/experiment_guide.md:378` records his standing role. The defect is double-credit, not invention.

**Fix:** Either drop both names from the Acknowledgments and add a Contributions statement, or move Dwayne off the byline if his contribution is the suggestion described. Confirm he has seen this specific draft — his recorded role is red-team auditing, and finding #1 is the kind of thing that role exists to catch.

### 10. MAJOR — Positional cross-references into a numbered list

`main.tex:42` "(see Limitation~1)", `main.tex:78` "(see Limitation~5)", `main.tex:319` etc. The Limitations are a bare `enumerate` with no `\label`s. These are hardcoded index references — the exact rot the check list names. Adding one limitation (e.g. the linear-attention confound from finding #7) silently repoints both.

**Fix:** `\item\label{lim:lens-mismatch}` / `\label{lim:single-null}` and cite via `\Cref{lim:...}`. This is required before finding #7's new limitation is inserted.

### 11. MINOR — PC1's ratio in `tab:pcs-l45` does not reproduce

`main.tex:263`: `PC1 & 0.004 & 0.002 & 1.8×`. 0.004/0.002 = **2.0**. Every other row reproduces exactly to the printed precision (PC2 2.258→2.3, PC3 0.2386→0.24, PC4 0.337→0.34, PC5 0.144→0.14, PC6 8.125→8.1, PC7 0.4, PC8 0.720→0.7, PC9 0.357→0.4, PC10 0.1096→0.1). PC1 is the only row where the printed numbers do not yield the printed ratio, which means the cosine and random columns are rounded harder than the others.

**Fix:** Print PC1's row to the precision the ratio needs (e.g. 0.0036 / 0.0020), or correct the ratio to 2.0×.

### 12. MINOR — The Researcher's Note carries superseded numbers

`main.tex:390`: "34--67\% of activation variance" — that is the `FINDINGS.md:53` figure. The abstract and §3.3 both say **28--67%**. The Note also says the workspace "excludes it **completely**," contradicting §3.3's L16 = 0.109, and "repeated **five** times across the sprint" against the abstract's **9** self-corrected claims. Same document, three stale figures.

**Fix:** 34→28, delete "completely," five→nine.

### 13. MINOR — Orphaned references and a title/URL mismatch

Rendered p.10: `[3] WeZZard` and `[4] Neuronpedia` print in the reference list but are cited nowhere in the text (Neuronpedia is named at `main.tex:61` and `main.tex:430` without `\cite`). Also `[2]`'s title says `jlens_qwenvl` while its URL is `github.com/jerrickhoang/jlens-qwen-jspace` — different repo slugs.

**Fix:** `\cite{neuronpedia2026}` at line 61 and `\cite{wezzard2026}` where the Apple Silicon implementation is relevant, or delete the entries. Reconcile [2]'s title against its URL.

### 14. MINOR — Gate failures are under-reported

`main.tex:110`: "45 of 63 layers pass ... L14 and L18--L23 fail criterion (b)." 63−45 = 18 failures; the named set is 7. L0–L10 (11 layers) also fail, on an unstated criterion, and the text's phrasing implies the named 7 are all of them.

**Fix:** "L0–L10 fail criterion (a); L14 and L18–L23 fail criterion (b)" — and state (a) and (b) explicitly, since neither is defined in the paper.

### 15. MINOR — Date, and a dropped redaction note

`\date{July 2026}` on an artifact last edited 2026-08-29 containing post-July material (C7, 9 falsified claims vs FINDINGS.md's 7). Separately, `DUAL_USE_REVIEW.md:31` requires that "the findings document includes a redaction note explaining that concurrent deception work exists but is disclosed separately." `FINDINGS.md:125` has it; **`main.tex` does not** — grep for `redact` returns zero hits in the paper. The venue-facing edition is the one that dropped it.

**Fix:** Update the date. Port the redaction note from `FINDINGS.md:125` into the paper.

---

## What I could not check

- **Every numeric value in the paper, against the measurements.** There is no code and no data for the ghost probe anywhere in this repository — I verified by glob for `*ghost*`, `*jlens*`, `*j_lens*`, `*jspace*` outside the paper directory: no files found. Findings #1, #3, and #5 rest on **document-vs-document contradictions** between `main.tex` and `FINDINGS.md`. Both are lab records, not raw output; a contradiction proves one is wrong but not which. To resolve I need the ghost-probe output (per-PC cosine, random baseline, and variance-matched baseline at L45 for PCs 1–10) and the C3 variance-matched script.
- **`main.aux`** — I could not read it; the read was blocked as a suspicious Windows path pattern. I verified label resolution from the rendered PDF instead (citations resolve to [1]–[4], no `[?]`), so this cost me nothing material.
- **Whether the four reference URLs resolve.** I did not make network requests. All four are dated June–July 2026 and two are GitHub repos that may have been renamed — note the [2] slug mismatch in finding #13. Needs a live fetch of all four.
- **The twin-edition comparison, as specified.** No twin exists: `ghost-dimensions/` has no `academic/` subdirectory, unlike most papers in this repo. I substituted `PAPER_DRAFT_v4.md` (the immediate markdown predecessor) and it is **in sync** with `main.tex` — controls table, `tab:pcs-l45` values, the PC6 dagger, `tab:falsified` row order and section placement, Limitations 7–10, and Data Availability all match line for line. The desync in this paper is not flight-vs-academic; it is **paper-vs-findings-record**.
- **Whether Dwayne Wilkes has signed off on this draft.** He is a real and consistently credited collaborator, but I found no review artifact for ghost-dimensions (other papers carry `AGNI_REVIEW.md` / `REVIEW_INDEX.md`; this directory has none). `FINDINGS.md:5` still reads "pending Agni adversarial review."
- **`main.pdf` staleness — checked and clean.** Sub-second timestamps: `main.tex` 23:21:55.979, `main.pdf` 23:21:59.691, and `main.log` records "Output written on main.pdf (10 pages, 368651 bytes)" matching the on-disk size exactly. The PDF is 4 seconds newer than its source and page 1 renders the current abstract text. Not a stale artifact. (Minute-granularity listings make it look inverted — it is not.)
